# cutver 0.21.0 — 2026-11-21

This is the first release that has to declare its own compatibility claim. A `minor` or `major` release
now refuses to run on a commit range that says nothing about compatibility, so a release can no longer
ship a break in silence — this release changes that contract, and its range says so. Alongside that
gate, three promises the project had already declared acquired the mechanism that keeps them: a
deprecated `cutver.toml` spelling warns instead of resolving quietly, a release body can live in the
tree and be reviewed before it is published, and the Windows replace that fails while another handle
holds the file is retried a bounded number of times instead of failing the release.

## Breaking changes

**A `minor` or `major` release refuses to run unless the commits it ships declare what it does about
compatibility** ([#357](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/357), closes
[#307](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/issues/307)). `cutver` compares the level against
`<previous_tag>..HEAD` and stops before anything is written, staged, committed or tagged when that range
carries neither declaration. The case it encodes is `0.19.0`: it shipped a plugin-environment contract
that broke every grant-less setup, no commit carried a footer, and silence was read as "compatible". A
`patch` release, a range with no commits and a repository with no previous tag are exempt. The refusal
reads `the minor release over 'v0.20.0..HEAD' declares no compatibility decision`
(`src/bump/types.rs:126`).

*To migrate*: add one of these to any commit inside the range the next time you cut a minor or major —
`BREAKING CHANGE: <migration>` or `BREAKING-CHANGE: <migration>` when the release breaks something,
`!` after the type (`feat(api)!: rewrite the parser`) for the same meaning, or
`NO-BREAKING-CHANGE: <why this release stays compatible>` when it does not. The first two reach the
notes as the warning block plus a `> **Migration**:` line; the third is provenance and never reaches
them.

## The release body comes from a file in the tree

[#343](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/343)

A release's notes can now live at `.github/releases/<tag>.md`, written in English and committed before
the dispatch, so the body is reviewed in the pull request that produced the release instead of existing
only on the release page — a published artifact a repository could not otherwise diff, review or roll
back from git. The tag comes from the step output, so the filename mapping is mechanical. Without the file the
template render is used, exactly as before: the convention is optional-with-fallback, because it adds an
authoring step per release. An empty file fails at the render step rather than falling back, so the
`--notes-file` refusal does not arrive after the publish phase has already spent its time.
`CHANGELOG.md` keeps the deterministic render, so `doctor --check-changelog` still means what it meant.
`v0.21.0` is the first release whose notes were written before its dispatch instead of backfilled
afterwards.

## Deprecated `cutver.toml` spellings warn instead of resolving silently

[#348](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/348), closes
[#272](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/issues/272)

Three `#[serde(alias)]` renames used to work without saying anything, which is the shape the contract
forbids — they keep working, and now they say so. The table holds `[version].source` (replaced by
`current_source`), `kind = "toml"` (by `"cargo-package"`) and `kind = "pyproject-toml"` (by
`"pyproject"`) (`src/config/deprecations.rs:47-66`). Each prints one sentence on stderr, never on
stdout, with or without `--json` — `warning: [version].source is deprecated, use current_source; it will
be removed in 1.0.0` — and, when CI is detected, the same line as a `::warning::` annotation. The exit
code does not move: a deprecation is not a failure, and an unknown key still fails closed with its
unchanged message. `doctor --json` gains `warnings`, one sentence per deprecated spelling and `[]` for a
canonical document; `init --update` reports the renames in the document it is about to rewrite.

## Fixes

- **A failed bump no longer leaves behind a `CHANGELOG.md` it created** ([#356](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/356),
  closes [#289](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/issues/289)): with `[changelog] path` declared and the
  file absent, the run generates it and the rollback now removes it, and neither `plan` nor a dry run
  fails where `bump` would have created it. An unreadable changelog still fails closed with its bytes
  preserved.
- **A Windows replace retries a held file instead of failing the release** ([#361](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/361),
  [#359](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/issues/359)): `MoveFileEx` with replace-existing answers
  `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` or `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` while another handle holds the destination — an
  editor, an indexer, an antivirus. The apply phase now makes three attempts, 20 ms apart, and only for
  those two codes; POSIX keeps a single attempt because its `rename` has no such failure mode. If the
  attempts are exhausted, the destination keeps its previous contents, the temporary file is removed and
  the error names both paths.

## Maintenance and documentation

- The required key set of every JSON surface is pinned per surface, so deleting a key in version 1 now
  fails a test ([#347](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/347)).
- The test suite no longer mutates the process environment: the environment is a seam, like the
  configuration lookups already were ([#351](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/351),
  [#354](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/354)).
- `CONTRACT.md` now classifies every judgement obligation it carries as inside or outside the 1.0
  freeze, with the reason, so the freeze's second reachability condition is decidable instead of
  assertable ([#355](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/355)).
- The reference pages gained a worked `cutver.toml` whose regex example actually captures
  ([#345](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/345)) and the enumerated release context keys a template
  can read ([#350](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/350)).

## What this release does not include

- Phases 5 and 6 of [#326](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/issues/326): `--channel` with promotion and
  `publish --resume`, plus declared per-phase needs and `--root`. The release transaction is complete
  through phase 4; those two are the freeze's third block.
- No test executes a workflow. The preference for `.github/releases/<tag>.md` is pinned by a contract
  test that reads the workflow file, not by a run, so this dispatch is the first thing that can exercise
  it — and the only evidence these notes will ever have that the file was picked up.
- A notes file whose name does not match the tag (`.github/releases/0.21.0.md` instead of `v0.21.0.md`)
  publishes the template render and only warns, naming the files that do exist.
- The `#![cfg(unix)]` suites do not run on a Windows host, so this release's local gate did not run
  them; CI's ubuntu and macOS legs did, and the Windows legs ran everything else.
- The Windows retry outlasts a collision measured in milliseconds. A destination held longer than the
  three-attempt window still fails closed by design, as
  [Pipeline execution & atomic guarantees](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/blob/main/docs/internals/pipeline.md#replace-rename-promise)
  states.
